trails.title: The whole flow
trails.subtitle: a host's call to a release, every trail in order
trails.say: One reply from end to end, a step for each stage: the host's call, the draft, the petition, the wait, the sealed ruling, the rules, the ledger and the release. Each step routes into the trails that tell it in depth.

steps.title: A host asks Blessed, not the model

entries.note: The one change a host makes: it calls Blessed where it called the model, and gets back only what a reviewer allowed.
entries.cite: WHAT

entries.note: Asks the wrapped model for its whole reply; any layer that speaks the chat-completions wire can answer.
entries.cite: doc:Blessed.blessed(_:)

steps.title: The draft is held as a petition

entries.anchor: try ledger.append(.submitted, petition: petition.id, digest: petition.digest, at: at)
entries.note: Checks the draft and its policy, keeps only the context the policy allows, stores the petition and writes its first ledger line.
entries.cite: test:submit trims the context, stores the petition and writes `submitted` with the draft's digest

steps.title: The caller waits, and a deadline may decide

entries.anchor: try await park(id, deadline: petition.policy.onLapse == .hold ? nil : petition.deadline)
entries.note: Suspends until the petition is decided; a cancelled caller leaves the review alone, and at a deadline the policy decides instead.
entries.cite: test:release suspends until a verdict lands

steps.title: A reviewer rules, with a seal

entries.note: On the reviewer's own device: a verdict pinned to the digest of the words they read, signed with their key.
entries.cite: WHAT

entries.anchor: let next = try petition.applying(verdict, at: at)
entries.note: The Gate checks the seal against the reviewer's public key, then applies the verdict.
entries.cite: test:decide refuses an unsealed or forged verdict under a sealing policy

entries.note: Withhold wins, blessings bind to the text, and stale or late verdicts are refused; at the quorum the petition is blessed.
entries.cite: WHAT

steps.title: Each transition is chained into the ledger

entries.note: Every transition writes one event, numbered and linked to the hash before it; the ledger holds digests and codes, never words.
entries.cite: test:a ledger holds ids, digests and codes; a withholding's reason never reaches it

steps.title: The release, issued once and checked

entries.anchor: guard let release = Release(petition: next, at: at) else { throw BlessError.notBlessed(petition.id) }
entries.note: The first caller to ask stamps the release and writes released; every waiter gets the same one.
entries.cite: test:two waiters get the same release, and it is logged once

entries.note: A release proves itself: its digest, every seal and the quorum are checked again from scratch.
entries.cite: test:quorum 2 through the Gate: one blessing waits, the second releases

trails.title: A reviewer's ruling
trails.subtitle: a sealed verdict to a release
trails.say: From the reviewer opening a petition to the release: the ruling is sealed on the reviewer's device, the Gate checks the seal, the rules decide, and the release is stamped once.

entries.anchor: try ledger.append(.viewed, petition: id, actor: reviewer, digest: petition.digest, at: at)
entries.note: Writes viewed with the reviewer and the digest of the text they opened.
entries.cite: test:pending lists by reviewer; markViewed writes `viewed` for reviewers only

steps.title: The ruling is sealed on the reviewer's device

entries.anchor: digest: petition.digest, note: note, issued: issued)
entries.note: Makes a verdict pinned to the digest of the petition's current text, and signs it with the reviewer's key.

entries.anchor: guard Seal.verify(verdict, verifyingKey: key) else { throw BlessError.badSeal(reviewer.id) }
entries.note: Verifies the verdict against the public key the petition names, and refuses an unsealed one when the policy requires seals.

entries.anchor: guard verdict.digest == current else { throw BlessError.staleVerdict(expected: current, saw: verdict.digest) }
entries.note: No stale verdicts, withhold wins, blessings bind to the text, one blessing per reviewer per text: each rule is a line here.
entries.cite: WHAT

entries.note: Counts only verdicts that endorse the current digest, once per reviewer; an amendment changes the digest, so the count starts again.
entries.cite: test:blessings bind to the text: an amendment starts the count again with the amender

entries.note: Announces the petition to observers and, once it is final, wakes every caller waiting on it.
entries.cite: test:two waiters get the same release, and it is logged once

entries.note: Stamps the release the first time it is handed out and writes released with its basis; later callers get the same release.
entries.cite: PIN

entries.note: Checks the release from scratch, the digest, every seal and the quorum, so a host can verify one it reads back.
entries.cite: test:quorum 2 through the Gate: one blessing waits, the second releases

trails.title: A deadline
trails.subtitle: the policy decides when no one answers
trails.say: From the deadline a policy sets to a lapse: a sweep finds what is due, the policy holds, withholds or sends its fallback, and a waiting caller wakes itself if no one sweeps.

entries.anchor: if let deadline, deadline <= .zero { throw BlessError.invalidPolicy("the deadline must be in the future") }
entries.note: A deadline must be in the future and a fallback must carry its text; both are checked when the petition is held.
entries.cite: test:a policy is validated against its reviewers

entries.note: Fixes the petition's deadline at submission, in whole milliseconds.
entries.cite: test:submit trims the context, stores the petition and writes `submitted` with the draft's digest

steps.title: A sweep lapses what is due

entries.anchor: for petition in try store.all() where petition.standing == .pending {
entries.note: Lapses every pending petition whose deadline has passed; the host runs it on its own schedule.
entries.cite: test:onLapse withhold: a sweep past the deadline expires it, wakes its waiter, and release throws expired

entries.anchor: try ledger.append(.expired, petition: id, digest: lapsed.digest, code: lapsed.policy.onLapse.name, at: at)
entries.note: Saves the lapsed petition and writes expired, with the policy's lapse as its code.
entries.cite: PIN

entries.note: Hold never lapses; withhold and a fallback end the petition as expired, and a lapse carries no verdict.
entries.cite: test:a lapse: hold never lapses; withhold and fallback expire it at the deadline, not before

entries.anchor: if case .releaseFallback(let text) = policy.onLapse, standing == .expired { return text }
entries.note: The only text a lapse can release is the policy's own, never the model's draft.
entries.cite: test:a fallback lapse releases the policy's text with basis lapsed and no verdicts

entries.note: Races the wait against a sleeper until the deadline, so a caller wakes even when no one sweeps.
entries.cite: test:a waiter with a deadline wakes itself when it passes, with no sweeper

trails.title: The seal
trails.subtitle: a signature over the exact words
trails.say: From a reviewer's key to a release that proves itself: the verdict's canonical bytes, an Ed25519 signature over them, its check at the Gate, and its check again at release.

entries.note: Rebuilds the reviewer from 32 raw bytes kept in the device's keychain; the Party it names carries only the public key.
entries.cite: PIN

entries.note: Everything in the verdict but the signature.
entries.cite: doc:Verdict.canonicalBytes

entries.note: bless/verdict/1: the petition, the reviewer, the ruling and its text, the digest read, the note and the time.
entries.cite: test:an amendment's canonical bytes carry its text and note, and match the golden vector

entries.note: CryptoKit's Ed25519 signs the bytes; its signatures are randomized, and each one verifies.
entries.cite: test:a verdict signed by its reviewer verifies

entries.note: Any RFC 8032 verifier accepts the signature, and one changed byte refuses it.
entries.cite: test:changing the text, the digest, the note or the time breaks the seal
